key_insight: Increasing deep-trap density in the p-type a-Si:H emitter degrades HIT cell performance by enhancing recombination, lowering built-in voltage, and can trigger S-shaped I-V behavior.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the emitter activation energy and deep-level defect density is critical to preserve Voc and fill factor in high-efficiency a-Si:H/c-Si heterojunction solar cells.
method: Simulated a-Si:H/c-Si HIT solar cells with AFORS-HET.
Varied the electronic density of states of the p-type a-Si:H emitter, especially deep dangling-bond traps.
Evaluated how defect density affects band bending, depletion region position, and I-V performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that once deep-trap density exceeds a critical value, Voc and fill factor drop sharply and an S-shaped I-V curve appears, consistent with strong recombination losses.
watch_item: The optimized performance depends sensitively on realistic emitter defect and activation-energy values, so fabrication variability could make the predicted optimum hard to reproduce.
paper_title: Effect of deep-trap density of states for a-Si:H layers on HIT cell performances: Modeling Framework
